findings.claim: The declared objective is final predicted target affinity as primary, with validity and strain secondary and coordinate control only; the reward view is the endpoint pointcloud with a detached FLOWR endpoint VJP, so coordinate contrasts are reward-relevant only through that endpoint path and are not physical interaction energies.

The observed window is the score-time grid 0.0 to 0.49 with learning window [0.0,0.5]; recorded affinities are removed and an equal score prior is used, so no decoded terminal affinity labels are available and last-record or survival credit cannot be presented as final affinity benefit.

Continuous contrast functions are only validated as observed-node linear interpolations: polynomial fits are not accepted and extrapolation is disallowed for the inspected landmark features, so any time-conditioned rule must stay inside the observed support and cannot be extrapolated.

The inspected landmark contrasts show sign reversals and strong sign conflicts across the window (e.g. landmark_00_soft_mass has 4 sign changes and 1 strong conflict; landmark_00_local_dx has 6 sign changes and 9 strong conflicts; landmark_00_local_dz has 10 sign changes and 7 strong conflicts), so a constant-sign coordinate rule is not supported by these curves and a time-conditioned rule would be required to track them.

Whole-window z values for the inspected landmark features are small and mixed in sign (e.g. soft_mass +0.64, local_dx -0.18, local_dy -0.30, local_dz -0.02, local_cxx -0.58, local_cyy -0.58), so the net whole-window marginal effect is weak and does not by itself justify prioritizing any single landmark coordinate.

hypotheses.direction: time-conditioned coordinate contrast at observed nodes
hypotheses.falsifier: a constant rule matching or exceeding the time-conditioned rule on independent-batch agreement, or the time-conditioned rule failing to reproduce the observed sign changes
hypotheses.observable: sign and rate of the landmark contrast curves across the observed window
hypotheses.scope: observed score times 0.0-0.49 only; no extrapolation
hypotheses.statement: A time-conditioned regional attention rule over observed score nodes, using the validated observed-node contrast curves rather than a constant rule, would better track the sign-reversing landmark contrasts than a static constant rule.

hypotheses.direction: prefer soft-mass landmark over local derivative landmarks
hypotheses.falsifier: independent-batch evidence showing the local derivative landmarks have larger, reproducible whole-window effects than soft_mass
hypotheses.observable: whole-window z and strong sign conflicts per landmark feature
hypotheses.scope: inspected landmark features in the observed window
hypotheses.statement: Prioritizing landmark_00_soft_mass over the local derivative landmarks is weakly supported at best, because its whole-window z is small and its curve reverses sign despite fewer conflicts than the local derivative features.

limitations: No decoded terminal affinity labels are supplied; recorded affinities are removed and an equal score prior is used, so final affinity benefit cannot be evaluated from the delivered evidence.

Only the first six continuous_trends rows were read; the remaining 194 rows and the branch_adjusted, endpoint_effects, increment_effects, joint_diagnostics, regional_effects, survival_effects and turnover_accounting tables were not inspected, so multiplicity-adjusted ranking and independent-batch counterexample checks are incomplete.
No joint or covariance diagnostics were read, so separation of local coordinate information from global pose/shape and any coupling claims remain unsupported.
Contrast curves are coordinate rewards through the endpoint VJP, not absolute reward targets or physical interaction energies; no neural-module causation is claimed.
